displayedInputs.question:
Two right circular cones with vertices facing down as shown in the figure below contain the same amount of liquid. The radii of the tops of the liquid surfaces are \(3\) cm and \(6\) cm. Into each cone is dropped a spherical marble of radius \(1\) cm, which sinks to the bottom and is completely submerged without spilling any liquid. What is the ratio of the rise of the liquid level in the narrow cone to the rise of the liquid level in the wide cone?

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

The figure is constructed from \(11\) line segments, each of which has length \(2.\) The area of pentagon \(ABCDE\) can be written as \(\sqrt m+\sqrt n,\) where \(m\) and \(n\) are positive integers. What is \(m+n?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

Let \(ABCD\) be an isosceles trapezoid having parallel bases \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{CD}\) with \(AB\gt CD.\) Line segments from a point inside \(ABCD\) to the vertices divide the trapezoid into four triangles whose areas are \(2,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) and \(5\) starting with the triangle with base \(\overline{CD}\) and moving clockwise as shown in the diagram below. What is the ratio \(\dfrac{AB}{CD}?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

Arjun and Beth play a game in which they take turns removing one brick or two adjacent bricks from one “wall” among a set of several walls of bricks, with gaps possibly creating new walls. The walls are one brick tall. For example, a set of walls of sizes \(4\) and \(2\) can be changed into any of the following by one move: \((3,2),\) \(\ (2,1,2),\) \(\ (4),\) \(\ (4,1),\) \(\ (2,2),\) or \((1,1,2).\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

Arjun plays first, and the player who removes the last brick wins. For which starting configuration is there a strategy that guarantees a win for Beth?

Let \(ABCD\) be a parallelogram with area \(15.\) Points \(P\) and \(Q\) are the projections of \(A\) and \(C,\) respectively, onto the line \(BD;\) and points \(R\) and \(S\) are the projections of \(B\) and \(D,\) respectively, onto the line \(AC.\) See the figure, which also shows the relative locations of these points.

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

Suppose \(PQ=6\) and \(RS=8,\) and let \(d\) denote the length of \(\overline{BD},\) the longer diagonal of \(ABCD.\) Then \(d^2\) can be written in the form \(m+n\sqrt p,\) where \(m,\) \(n,\) and \(p\) are positive integers and \(p\) is not divisible by the square of any prime. What is \(m+n+p?\)

As shown in the figure below, point \(E\) lies in the opposite half-plane determined by line \(CD\) from point \(A\) so that \(\angle CDE = 110^\circ.\) Point \(F\) lies on \(\overline{AD}\) so that \(DE=DF,\) and \(ABCD\) is a square. What is the degree measure of \(\angle AFE?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

A farmer’s rectangular field is partitioned into a \(2\) by \(2\) grid of \(4\) rectangular sections as shown in the figure. In each section the farmer will plant one crop: corn, wheat, soybeans, or potatoes. The farmer does not want to grow corn and wheat in any two sections that share a border, and the farmer does not want to grow soybeans and potatoes in any two sections that share a border. Given these restrictions, in how many ways can the farmer choose crops to plant in each of the four sections of the field?

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

What is the area of the shaded figure shown below?

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)
